Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

taste verb

also taste like, taste of, it tastes of, sense of taste, not to my taste

classical

gustō, gustāre, gustāvī, gustātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Other words

  • sapiō, sapere, sapīvī — taste of, have a flavour

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive; with an accusative, taste of something · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 2.6.104: occīsam saepe sapere plūs multō suem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 73 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Said of the food, not of the person tasting, with an accusative of what it tastes of. To taste something oneself is gustāre.

  • gustātus, gustātūs m. — the sense of taste

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.141 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 59 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Hoc gustā.

    Taste this.composed

  • Gustā. Placetne tibi?

    Taste it. Do you like it?composed

  • sapere (+ acc.)

    taste likeTraupman 73

  • Hoc nōn meī stomachī est.

    This is not to my taste.Traupman 390

See also flavour, eat.
